Icon Scales & Legends

Source: vignettes/articles/scales-and-legends.Rmd
scales-and-legends.Rmd

This article covers mapping data to icons, and explaining those icons with legends. It uses the same port_talbot data as Getting Started:

library(leaflet)
library(leaf.magic)

port_talbot$open_year <- as.integer(format(port_talbot$start_date, "%Y"))
port_talbot$popup <- paste0(
  "<strong>", toupper(port_talbot$site), "</strong> (", port_talbot$code, ")",
  "<hr>Site Type: ", port_talbot$site_type,
  "<br>Opened: ", port_talbot$open_year
)

Icon Scales

leaf.magic has three functions for mapping data to icons, which are the icon equivalents of leaflet’s colour functions:

Icons Colours Data
iconFactor() colorFactor() Categories
iconBin() colorBin() Numbers, split into bins
iconQuantile() colorQuantile() Numbers, split into quantiles

Each takes some icons and a domain, and returns a function which turns data into icon names.

site_types <- c("Urban Industrial", "Urban Background", "Urban Traffic")

# like leaflet::colorFactor(), levels are sorted alphabetically:
# "Urban Background", "Urban Industrial", "Urban Traffic"
iconPal <- iconFactor(
  icons = c("house", "industry", "car"),
  domain = site_types
)

iconPal(c("Urban Traffic", "Urban Background"))
#> [1] "car"   "house"
leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type)
    )
  )

iconBin() and iconQuantile() map numeric data to icons. In this case, it makes most sense to choose icons that have some inherent “order” to them.

These functions take the same arguments as colorFactor(), colorBin() and colorQuantile() and split the data in exactly the same way, so if you give an icon function and a colour function the same settings (and the same number of icons as colours), every level gets a consistent icon-colour pair. They are also icon-led - the bins and n arguments default to the length of the provided icons, so you don’t need to specify them if you’re happy letting the functions decide the break-points/probs for you.

iconPalYr <- iconQuantile(
  icons = c("hourglass-start", "hourglass-half", "hourglass-end"),
  domain = port_talbot$open_year
)

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPalYr(open_year)
    )
  )

Icon scales don’t just work for icons - they map data to any set of names. For example, they can map data to marker shapes, or to text for text markers.

Icon Legends

addIconLegend() constructs icon legends. It works just like leaflet::addLegend(): give it an icon scale as pal along with the values used on the map, and it works out the icons and labels for you. Icon and colour legends can be used side-by-side.

catPal <- colorFactor(c("#12436D", "#28A197", "#801650"), domain = site_types)
yearPal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = port_talbot$open_year)

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ yearPal(open_year)
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    pal = yearPal,
    values = ~open_year,
    title = "Opening Year",
    labFormat = labelFormat(big.mark = "")
  ) |>
  addIconLegend(
    pal = iconPal,
    values = ~site_type,
    title = "Site Type"
  )

Combined Legends

Often, the colour of the marker (or icon) and the icon itself will align. In that case, a colour scale can be passed to the colors argument of addIconLegend() to create an efficient, combined legend. As long as the icon and colour scales share the same settings, every icon is paired with the right colour.

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)
    )
  ) |>
  addIconLegend(
    pal = iconPal,
    values = ~site_type,
    colors = catPal,
    title = "Site Type"
  )

This also works for numeric scales; for example, an iconQuantile() scale gives one legend item per quantile.

# colorQuantile() defaults to n = 4, so match the 3 icons of iconPalYr
colPalYr <- colorQuantile(
  c("#12436D", "#28A197", "#801650"),
  domain = port_talbot$open_year,
  n = 3
)

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPalYr(open_year),
      markerColor = ~ colPalYr(open_year)
    )
  ) |>
  addIconLegend(
    pal = iconPalYr,
    values = ~open_year,
    colors = colPalYr,
    title = "Opening Year"
  )

Manual Legends

Legends can also be built by hand with the icons, labels and colors arguments, and - like leaflet::addLegend() - shown and hidden alongside a layer using group.

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)
    ),
    group = "Sites"
  ) |>
  addIconLegend(
    icons = c("industry", "car", "house"),
    labels = c("Industrial", "Traffic", "Background"),
    colors = c("#28A197", "#801650", "#12436D"),
    title = "Site Type",
    group = "Sites"
  ) |>
  addLayersControl(
    overlayGroups = "Sites",
    options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)
  )

Attribution

If you use leaf.magic, you may want to add an attribution to Font Awesome or one of the other icon providers (set using library). addIconAttribution() is a convenient way to do this, and even comes with its own group and layerId options for precise “layer” control. Try toggling the breweries on and off in the example below.

leaflet(breweries91) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(icon = magicIcons("beer", "red"), group = "Breweries") |>
  addIconAttribution(group = "Breweries") |>
  addLayersControl(
    overlayGroups = "Breweries",
    options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)
  )
